riparian areas are important for the provision of water quality regulation, but that their contribution may be less than previously assumed, particularly in less intensive agricultural systems.
riparian areas, although not always distinct from neighbouring areas, do have a role in providing ecosystem services.

riparian areas in agricultural catchments are not necessarily more functional than non-riparian areas, however, riparian areas in more natural catchments (e.g. forested catchments) may have an important role in water quality regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the functioning of the riparian zone is highly habitat specific and that the riparian zone may not necessarily be more important than the surrounding land in terms of water quality regulation.

riparian areas are not necessarily more productive or efficient in terms of ecosystem services provision than surrounding non-riparian habitats, however, they are likely to be more resilient to disturbance, and thus may be more important in the long term.
riparian areas are a mosaic of habitats, each delivering a range of ecosystem services to different extents.
